name: Exemplifying Such As
pattern: Nom or NP + such as + example XP or coordination

entry.name: Exemplifying Such As
entry.pattern: Nom or NP + such as + example XP or coordination

1.definition: Introduces one or more illustrative members of the class just described.

examples.form: Bring safety gear [such as gloves and goggles].

projection.target: The examples do not exhaust the class. Other suitable safety gear can meet the instruction without being on the example list.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Giving examples with such as
curious.summary: Such as introduces some examples of the kind of thing you've just named.
curious.body:
In Bring safety gear such as gloves and goggles, such as introduces examples of safety gear. The phrase is an offer of illustration, not a full list.

That means other safety gear can still meet the instruction. Someone who brings a helmet hasn't ignored the request just because a helmet wasn't in the list.

This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and rests on one constructed illustration.

examples.text: Bring safety gear [such as gloves and goggles].
We need fruit [such as apples and pears].

curious.try: Write a sentence naming a kind of thing, then add such as and two examples. Could something not on your list still count?

teacher.summary: Useful for explaining how such as introduces examples without listing everything.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a noun or NP followed by such as and one or more illustrative members of the class just described, given as a phrase or coordination. The examples do not exhaust the class: other suitable safety gear can meet the instruction without being on the example list. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and rests on one constructed illustration. It lists same-as comparison and integrated relative modifiers as related patterns in separate entries.
teacher.terms: Exemplification is the term the cited grammar uses for this role.

examples.text: Bring safety gear [such as gloves and goggles].
We need fruit [such as apples and pears].

watch_for: A learner might read the examples after such as as a complete list.
A learner might think a helmet wouldn't count in the safety gear example because it isn't listed.
teacher.activity: Students write instructions that name a class and give examples with such as, for example "Pack warm clothes such as ...". A partner suggests another item that fits the class but isn't on the list.

child.hook: When you say such as, do you name everything?
child.explain: Such as lets you name a few examples. It doesn't have to name everything. Other things of the same kind can fit too.

examples.text: Bring snacks [such as apples and crackers].
Bring safety gear [such as gloves and goggles].

child.play: Name a group, like pets or fruit. Say it with such as and two examples. Then a friend adds one more thing that fits.
